---
title: "How can I explore whether a time series is reasonably stable?"
---

## What the question asks

How can I explore whether a time series is reasonably stable?

## Steps to decide and solve

Inspect a time plot; compare the mean and spread in similar early and late windows; look for trend, variance changes and dependence.

## Worked example: Nile

```{r}
#| eval: false
d <- ru_data("Nile")
check <- ru_apply("stationarity", data=d, x="flow", time="year")
stopifnot(nrow(check)==2L)
```

Window means and sample standard deviations describe the earlier and later sections of the records. They are diagnostic clues, not a definitive test that the generating process is stationary.

## Apply it to another question

```r
ru_apply("stationarity", data=your_data, x="numeric_column", time="date_column")
```

Stable variance alone does not imply a constant mean; stable means alone do not establish unchanging autocorrelation.

Use `ru_plan("stationarity")` to inspect alternative routes when required information is absent or uncertain.
